instrument: tools/ascent/roof_rungs.py (G007), re-run by the controller against the POST-reconstruction Q80 numbers I verified myself

q80_mixed_1p5.VERDICT: Q80 does NOT need more density to reach 50 OR 100 TPS. At its current 2.218 GB/token the roof is 185.5 TPS and rung B is reachable on bytes alone. It sits at 1.8% of that roof. The lever is execution efficiency, not BPW. Only rung C (200 TPS) is byte-blocked, and only just - it needs 2.06 GB against the current 2.218.

qwen38.note: OPPOSITE regime. Bandwidth-bound at 406.2 of 411.51 GB/s = 98.7% of ceiling, so it has no execution headroom and BPW is its ONLY lever. Corrected projections with fixed 1.415 ms overhead: 2.0 BPW -> 58.2 TPS, 1.5 -> 75.5, 1.25 -> 88.7.

THE_STRATEGIC_SPLIT: The two lead models need OPPOSITE work and it is now measured on both sides. Q80: 1.8% of its roof, density irrelevant until rung C, fix execution. Qwen3.8: 98.7% of ceiling, execution maxed, fix density. Applying either model's lever to the other wastes the lane.
physical_limit_discipline: Neither model is at a physical limit. Q80 is at 14.7% of the decode ceiling on GPU and 1.8% of roof on wall. Per S004 s4 a physical-limit claim requires naming the saturated hardware resource; nothing here saturates one.
